extracted.intended_audience: printers, publishers, typographers, book designers, librarians, booklovers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for designing, producing, proofreading, and judging books (typography, paper, binding, format, ornament, and legibility). Aimed at improving both aesthetic and utilitarian qualities of printed books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of the book
rubrics_metrics.description: The book's constituent elements as a basis for judgment and construction (identified as 'elements of the book' on pages 4-6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes type, paper, binding, illustrations, margins, edges, ink, and finishing. Each element contributes to the book's utility, expression, beauty, and structural character; evaluate a book by considering these parts together rather than singly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fitness in book design
rubrics_metrics.description: Fitness in book design: the appropriateness of form to function and content ('Fitness in book design,' 9-13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design choices (type, size, ornament, paper, format) should be appropriate to the subject and use of the book. A book should express its content by suitable typographic and material decisions rather than adopting a one-size-fits-all treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: The book beautiful (esthetics)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The book beautiful' — the aesthetic aspect of a book as an art object (discussed at length under 'The book beautiful', 49-62).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauty involves harmony among elements (type, paper, binding, decoration) and should be pursued without defeating utility. The beautiful book obeys laws of esthetics while still being serviceable and not necessarily expensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legibility (types and eyes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legibility as a primary criterion: progress in legibility, the relation of types to human eyesight, and factors affecting readable print ('Types and eyes: The problem,' 120-127; 'Progress,' 128-133).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess typeface, size, contrast, ink, paper tint, leading, tracking, line length, and page color for legibility. Empirical studies (Javal, Cattell, Sanford, Clark University) inform choices. Use occlusion/oculist-style tests and consider near-sight prevalence among readers (children, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to the rule of legibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgement that aesthetic or expressive aims sometimes justify departures from strict legibility ('Exceptions to the rule of legibility,' 130-138).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize legitimate exceptions (e.g., tribute typography, highly decorative volumes) where expressive effect or historical reproduction may override ordinary legibility metrics; but these should be conscious, not accidental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of typeface
rubrics_metrics.description: Type selection should suit subject and expressiveness (numerous endorsements and cautions regarding Bodoni, Caslon, Cloister Oldstyle, Century, Kennerley, Cheltenham, New Humanistic, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose types that harmonize with content and intended reader: safe norms for poetry (Cloister Oldstyle), humanistic forms for literature, highly contrasted types (Bodoni) for elegance but with attention to legibility. Examples of recommended faces and their appropriate uses are given throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast, ink and paper tint
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast between type and background (ink color and paper tint) affects legibility and expression (e.g., buff-tinted or blue-tinted paper noted as beneficial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select ink and paper tint that reduce glare and increase comfort; blue or buff tints may help the eye. Consider which ink is 'best for the eye' and how contrast shapes the book's expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leading and spacing (including hyphenation and line endings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Line spacing (leading), interline spacing, indentation, and hyphenation practices affect readability and appearance ('Leading' and 'Indenting', 'Line endings should not show too many hyphens').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide adequate leading for the chosen type size; avoid cramped spacing and excessive hyphenation at line ends. Manage indentation and initial spacing (mitering of initials) so they harmonize with text flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of line and column width
rubrics_metrics.description: Normal/optimal line length for legibility and the use of columns in wide pages ('Columns, in wide pages'; 'Length of line, normal length for legibility').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly long lines; use appropriate columnization if page width would harm readability. Design line length with eye comfort and rhythm in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page proportions and margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportions of the page and margins as determinants of visual balance and function ('Page, proportions of,' 'Margin, size and proportions of').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose margin sizes and overall page proportions that balance text block and white space; consider diagonal of page and traditional proportion rules for an agreeable effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding and 'the clothing of a book'
rubrics_metrics.description: Binding as a key element of the book's physical and aesthetic identity ('Binding, as an element of the book'; 'The clothing of a book,' 97-101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess materials (cloth, leather, parchment), decoration, durability, and appropriateness to the book's purpose. Avoid unnecessary rebindings that waste resources; binding should protect and express the book without needlessly increasing cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finishing, edges and gilding
rubrics_metrics.description: Edge treatment, finishing, and decorative choices (gilding, goffered edges) as part of the book's craftsmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use finishing details (gilding, edge treatment) that suit the volume's character. Ornament should be tasteful and subordinate to the book's function and style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initials, ornamentation and decoration
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and spacing of initials and decoration (colored initials, mitering, illumination) as expressive elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate initials and ornament so they aid readability and aesthetic effect. Ensure spacing and mitering are executed with attention to proportion and legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations and fitness with type
rubrics_metrics.description: Fitness between illustrations and type: illustrations are elements of the book and must be appropriate to type and content ('Fitness, between illustrations and type').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harmonize style, scale, and placement of illustrations with typeface and page design. Illustrations should enhance rather than compete with text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper choice, thickness and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials of the book: paper vs parchment vs papyrus; 'Thick paper and thin' and choices affecting bulk, lightness, and durability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select paper quality and thickness based on desired bulk, durability, and handling characteristics. Thin papers (Oxford India) can give lightness; thick paper may be deceptive in heft. Consider three elements of paper (surface, color, and substance) and historical materials (bamboo, palm, parchment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bulk, size, and favorite book sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: The book's physical size and bulk (favorite book sizes; 'The book of to-day and the book of to-morrow'; compactness and legibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt sizes appropriate to the book's use and reader: small, handier formats are often preferable for daily reading; bulk should be economical for libraries and readers. Measure trade-offs between size, cost, legibility, and portability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economics and democratization of books
rubrics_metrics.description: Economics of book production: books are subject to economic laws; cost vs beauty ('Economics, the book within the domain of, 115,116'; democratization by cheap Aldine books).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance aesthetic aims with cost considerations—well-made and beautiful books need not be exorbitantly priced. Design choices should consider public access and the goal of democratizing learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing process, 'spoilers' and quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: Roles and potential faults of production participants (compositor, binder, papermaker, ink-maker, printer) who can 'spoil' a book ('Binder, a spoiler of books'; 'Compositor, a spoiler'; 'Papermaker, a spoiler', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain rigorous quality control across production: check composition, ink, paper, and binding. Printers and publishers must oversee vendors to prevent spoilage of otherwise good design and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading, author revisions and corrigenda
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofs, author revision in proof, and post-publication correction practices ('authors rewriting in proof' exemplified by Balzac and Carlyle; 'Corrigenda', 'Errata').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage careful proofreading and author engagement with proofs to minimize misprints. When errors occur, provide clear corrigenda/errata lists; understand that proof correction is a critical stage in ensuring the book's integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors of the press and handling misprints
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'perversities of type': causes, consequences, and social effects of misprints; types of misprints such as indecency, ghost words, and serious blunders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and guard against misprints through proofreading, compositors' care, and corrected editions. Maintain archives of errata and correct public records when misprints have reputational or legal consequences (examples cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification and typographic rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements of justification and typographic conventions for setting text ('Justification, requirements of, 58, 59').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply justification practices that preserve even spacing, avoid rivers and excessive word-spacing, and control hyphenation. Use typographic judgment to balance evenness with legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretative/expression in typography
rubrics_metrics.description: Typography as an interpreter of meaning: 'interpretative typography' and 'expression in typography' (9-13, 137-138).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use typographic features (typeface, spacing, ornament, color) to reflect and interpret the tone, period, or subject of the work—without undermining clarity except where deliberately intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests of utility and reading guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Testing a book's practical utility for readers and the need to educate book buyers ('tests of its utility', 'Book buyers, how to educate').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate books not only for appearance but for how well they serve readers (ease of reading, portability, selection). Publishers and librarians should help educate buyers toward better choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactness, lightness, and deceptive weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of compactness and lightness in book design: thin-paper editions, perceived 'lightness' vs real bulk ('Lightness, in books, deceptive', 'Thick paper and thin').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use paper and format to achieve desirable compactness without sacrificing durability or legibility. Beware that perceived lightness may mask poor construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favorite literature matched with appropriate typography
rubrics_metrics.description: Match canonical or 'favorite' literature with typographic treatment suited to its character ('Favorite literature, in appropriate typography').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design editions with a sensitivity to the author's style and the book's cultural place—e.g., poetry may favor certain types and spacing; classics may warrant restrained, dignified typography.
